import pytz
from dateutil.parser import parse

# Constants
TIME_FORMAT = "%d/%m/%y %H:%M:%S.%f"

def task_func(time_string, from_tz, to_tz):
    from_zone = pytz.timezone(from_tz)
    to_zone = pytz.timezone(to_tz)

    dt = parse(time_string, dayfirst=True)

    if dt.tzinfo is None:
        dt = from_zone.localize(dt, is_dst=None)
    else:
        dt = dt.astimezone(from_zone)

    converted = dt.astimezone(to_zone)
    return converted.strftime(TIME_FORMAT)[:-3]

issues: Uses dateutil.parser.parse without dayfirst=True even though the required format is dd/mm/yy, so ambiguous dates like 03/04/24 may be parsed incorrectly.
localize() is called without is_dst=None, so ambiguous daylight-saving times may be silently resolved to one offset instead of being detected.
If the parsed input already contains timezone information, localize() will raise ValueError because pytz.localize expects a naive datetime.
